incidents.title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
incidents.summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an elaborate artificial intelligence scam. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos impersonating him to defraud vulnerable immigrants. In these deepfakes, a digital version of Leal promotes fraudulent immigration services, including offering US residency assistance for $2,200 to undocumented immigrants without deportation orders. The scams typically direct victims through social media videos to contact phone numbers via WhatsApp, where fraudsters send fake contracts and collect payments through digital payment apps like Venmo and Zelle.

Leal discovered the scheme last October when potential clients began calling his office, but the situation has dramatically worsened in recent months. His firm hired an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across multiple platforms: 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scam also features AI-generated testimonials from supposed former clients praising Leal's services. He has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the fraud's origin.

incidents.title: ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception
incidents.summary:
# Summary

A fake online article falsely depicted Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock in a heated interview with ABC finance presenter Alan Kohler, where she supposedly objected to questions about Boulder Sparhaven, an unlicensed cryptocurrency trading platform. The article never actually happened but exemplifies a rising scam trend that ASIC says is becoming increasingly sophisticated thanks to artificial intelligence. Scammers are creating fake deepfake images and videos of well-known Australians, including Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Gina Rinehart, and Alan Kohler himself, to promote fraudulent investment schemes.

According to new ASIC research released today, investment scams have exploded in prevalence and complexity. Last year, ASIC removed 19,400 scams, up 182 percent, including 5,476 phishing scams and 7,051 fake investment platforms. Scammers build elaborate webs of deception using fabricated news articles, fake websites, and bogus reviews to lure victims who provide personal details and eventually money. ASIC urges consumers to verify Australian Financial Services licence numbers through official registers, while Kohler argues that platforms hosting such content should face heavy fines.

incidents.title: Sleep Staging Is Not Guesswork
incidents.summary:
A class-action lawsuit has been filed against Oura, the smart ring company, by the Clarkson Law Firm in San Francisco. The suit alleges that Oura engaged in false advertising regarding its sleep tracking technology. The company markets rings priced at $300 and higher by claiming they can track sleep stages with 95% accuracy, comparable to hospital sleep labs. However, the lawsuit contends that Oura's devices cannot accurately measure the physiological signals needed for precise sleep tracking and instead rely on unreliable artificial intelligence estimates no better than random guesses.

Oura has responded by defending its science and citing peer-reviewed research validating its sleep staging accuracy. The company noted that while Oura Ring is not a medical device, its technology has been compared favorably against polysomnography in multiple studies. The lawsuit seeks class action status and a jury trial, though it remains unclear what compensation affected customers might receive or whether they can join the suit. This is not Oura's first legal challenge, as the company is also facing another ongoing class action alleging unauthorized collection of personal information.

incidents.title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that the Aurora ransomware group has been active since April 2026 and developed a Linux variant designed to target ESXi environments. The group operated a data leak site and targeted organizations across multiple countries. Researchers found that Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation attacks against ten target organizations between April 8 and May 21, 2026. The ESXi ransomware encrypts virtual machine files while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can read ransom demands, and includes specialized modes for targeting specific environments.

The investigation identified two distinct clusters of Aurora activity. The first cluster used custom tools like esxi_finder.py to locate ESXi hosts and vCenter servers on victim networks, then deployed the ransomware via manual copying. Operators placed strict restrictions on the AI agent, forbidding certain techniques like DCSync attacks and account lockouts. A second Aurora cluster, attributed with medium confidence to potentially different operators, used different tactics including SQL Server exploitation and S3 data exfiltration across eight victim organizations in six countries.

incidents.title: A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries
incidents.summary:
A major Pizza Hut franchisee filed a lawsuit in Texas alleging that Pizza Hut's AI-powered delivery system called Dragontail caused over $100 million in damages to its business. Chaac Pizza Northeast, which operates approximately 111 Pizza Hut locations across the Northeast, claims the system created cascading operational problems after being rolled out in 2024. The company says that before the system, over 90 percent of its deliveries arrived within 30 minutes and sales were growing at double-digit rates, but performance sharply declined afterward.

According to the lawsuit, Dragontail gave DoorDash drivers real-time visibility into kitchen operations, allowing them to see when pizzas were ready. This caused drivers to wait up to fifteen minutes to batch multiple orders together rather than delivering immediately, significantly slowing delivery times and reducing customer satisfaction. The suit also claims drivers could see tip amounts and payment methods, making them less likely to accept certain orders. In New York City specifically, year-over-year sales dropped from positive 10.19 percent to negative 9.78 percent after implementation. Pizza Hut declined to comment beyond stating it would respond through legal channels.

incidents.title: Inside the Fake Celebrity Podcast Scam Fooling Hollywood
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Scammers are impersonating Terry Gross and other staff members of NPR's "Fresh Air" program to defraud people seeking media appearances. The fraudulent emails target authors, entertainers and public figures with highly personalized messages that reference their work and offer interview opportunities. Recipients are eventually asked to pay fees, typically around $250, for supposed production costs. WHYY, NPR and law enforcement are investigating the scheme, which has also targeted other celebrities like comedians Nikki Glaser and Amy Poehler.

Experts attribute the scam's effectiveness to artificial intelligence, which allows criminals to create convincing, personalized impersonations at low cost. Red flags include requests for money, emails from suspicious addresses like terrygrossfreshair@gmail.com, and the unusual scenario of a major show's host personally handling booking logistics. WHYY clarified it never charges guests for interviews. Cybersecurity specialists recommend verifying interview invitations through legitimate organizational contacts rather than responding to suspicious messages, and note that AI-enabled scams are becoming increasingly sophisticated and harder to detect.

incidents.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Israeli-funded operators created a fake American think tank called the Hanover Institute to influence artificial intelligence systems into promoting pro-Israel arguments. Between August 6 and 14, the website published 124 reports totaling over 560,000 words designed to appear as neutral academic research on topics including Israeli military actions, Palestinian casualties, and genocide accusations. The operation used a commercial platform optimized to make chatbots cite the content, and filed disclosures under US foreign agent law. The institute has no legal existence, physical address, or named staff, and funding that was initially denied was later acknowledged after the scheme became public.

The campaign represents part of a broader Israeli government effort worth tens of millions of dollars routed through intermediaries including European advertising firm Havas Media. Israeli officials have expressed frustration that such spending has failed to improve Israel's standing in American public opinion, with recent polling showing Americans increasingly sympathetic to Palestinians. Researchers warn the operation demonstrates a new threat of AI manipulation by foreign governments, though the campaign's success at influencing chatbot responses has not translated into changing public opinion polls.

incidents.title: Round Hill is suing Suno and Anthropic for up to $1B apiece. It isn’t looking to settle.
incidents.summary:
Major record labels, including Universal Music Group, Sony Music, Warner Music, Capitol Records, and Atlantic Records, have sued two popular AI music generators called Udio and Suno. The labels accuse both companies of scraping thousands of copyrighted songs without permission to train their AI models and then generating new music that directly reproduces sections of famous recordings. The lawsuits were filed in New York against Udio and in Massachusetts against Suno, where the companies are based. The record labels submitted a massive list of thousands of specific copyrighted works they claim were used illegally, including songs from artists like The Beatles, Michael Jackson, Mariah Carey, and Bruce Springsteen.

To support their claims, the record labels demonstrated they could recreate famous songs by inputting specific prompts into both AI music generators. For example, using prompts describing Chuck Berry's style generated outputs that closely mimicked "Johnny B. Goode," and a prompt about Mariah Carey produced a near identical version of "All I Want for Christmas Is You." Both Udio and Suno have refused to disclose which music trained their models, claiming their use of copyrighted material constitutes fair use. The lawsuits represent a major legal battle about generative AI services and copyright protection.

incidents.title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio
incidents.summary:
Universal Music Group has reached a settlement with AI music startup Udio, resolving a lawsuit that accused Udio of using copyrighted songs to train its artificial intelligence model. The company uses AI to generate original music from text prompts. Under the agreement, Udio will launch a new platform next year that operates only with authorized and licensed music, allowing users to customize, stream and share their creations. UMG, which owns rights to songs like The Temptations' "My Girl," had alleged that Udio illegally used such copyrighted tracks to create similar melodies.

This settlement marks Udio's first licensing agreement with a major music label. The startup, founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind employees and backed by investors including will.i.am, has attracted millions of users since its launch. Under the new arrangement, artists can opt into the platform and receive compensation, though Udio declined to disclose specific financial terms or compensation details. UMG also announced a separate partnership with Stability AI to develop music creation tools for artists and producers.

incidents.title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings
incidents.summary:
# Summary

State Farm's defense lawyers apologized after attorneys discovered that artificial intelligence had generated fake legal cases, nonexistent quotes, and fabricated legal holdings in court filings. The case involves Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga, who sued State Farm after a 2020 fire made her Carson home uninhabitable, followed by water damage during repairs. She claimed State Farm delayed approving repairs, leaving the work incomplete and causing her family to exhaust savings, declare bankruptcy, and lose their home to foreclosure. Lawyer Jacquelene Robinson admitted using an AI tool called Irys to prepare motions, resulting in seven fake case citations across eight filings, incorrect case titles, and misquoted passages.

The incident highlights a growing problem in the legal field, where 41 percent of law firms now use artificial intelligence. A Paris-based researcher has documented nearly 1,900 cases of legal AI hallucinations worldwide, primarily in the United States. Last year, a California attorney received a record ten thousand dollar fine for submitting a brief with twenty-one fabricated quotes from ChatGPT. Meni-Siliga's case is scheduled for trial in October, and State Farm stated it expects external counsel to meet the highest ethical standards.

stories.Headline: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia Extend Partnership in AI and Data
stories.Summary:
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have agreed to deepen their cooperation in artificial intelligence, data governance, and emerging technologies. The agreement was announced following a meeting between Pakistan's Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja and Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority President Abdullah bin Sharaf Alghamdi at the LEAP 2026 conference in Riyadh. The two nations plan to establish a comprehensive and long-term technology partnership.

During the discussion, Pakistan's minister outlined the country's national AI and data governance initiatives while reaffirming Pakistan's commitment to building a strong data ecosystem and growing its digital economy. Both countries intend to collaborate on emerging technologies and create a lasting framework for cooperation. The partnership reflects a broader regional focus on advancing artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure, technology skills, and data-driven development.

stories.Headline: Datametrex Plans to Focus on AI, Data Centre, and Patent Licensing
stories.Summary:
Datametrex AI Limited announced plans to shut down its healthcare operations to focus on artificial intelligence, data centre technology, and patent licensing. The company operates medical clinics in Edmonton, Calgary, and Vancouver, British Columbia, providing primary and emergency care services. The gradual wind-down aims to streamline the corporate structure, reduce operating costs and regulatory requirements, and improve financial performance by redirecting resources toward core business areas.

The company will manage the transition carefully, considering operational, financial, contractual, and regulatory factors. Management plans to assess opportunities to maximize value from healthcare assets during the process. The strategic shift allows Datametrex to concentrate capital and resources on artificial intelligence and data centre initiatives, which align with long-term objectives. The company indicated it would provide further updates as developments occur.

stories.Headline: Oklahoma State University adds new AI, logistics programs for fall semester
stories.Summary:
Oklahoma State University Institute of Technology is launching two new academic programs beginning in fall 2026. The first is a 60-credit-hour online Associate in Applied Science in Logistics and Supply Chain Technology that students can complete in four to five semesters. This program covers warehousing, transportation, inventory management, and data-informed decision-making, preparing graduates for careers as logistics coordinators, distribution center managers, inventory specialists, and supply chain coordinators. The second offering is an Applied Artificial Intelligence option within the existing Bachelor of Technology in Information Technologies program.

The university designed both programs to address workforce demands in Oklahoma and beyond. The logistics program prepares students for industry-recognized credentials that can lead to over 11 million jobs nationwide. The artificial intelligence program goes beyond teaching tool usage, instead focusing on applying AI technologies to solve real organizational problems while considering ethics and governance. OSUIT Provost Dr. Richie Roberts stated that preparing students with skills aligned to industry needs helps build a strong workforce supporting the state's economic growth.

stories.Headline: Mark Cuban Foundation and Tonic Bring Free AI Bootcamp to Denver Teens
stories.Summary:
The Mark Cuban Foundation and Tonic are offering a free artificial intelligence bootcamp to high school students in Denver this fall. The program is open to ninth through twelfth graders and will run over three consecutive Saturdays on October 31, November 7, and November 14. All costs including meals, transportation, and technology will be covered for participants at no charge. Applications close on September 30.

The bootcamp provides hands-on experience with AI tools and explores real-world applications across fields like healthcare, business, sports science, and career preparation. Students will work on a capstone project guided by industry mentors. This Denver bootcamp is one of more than 35 similar programs being hosted across the United States by various companies. Mark Cuban emphasized the importance of providing AI education to underserved students to prepare them for future educational and employment opportunities.

stories.Headline: Brazil's electoral court sets new standards for AI deepfakes after case involving Sen. Bolsonaro
stories.Summary:
Brazil's electoral court established new standards for identifying artificial intelligence-generated deepfakes in political advertising as the country prepares for October elections. The ruling came from a case involving opposition candidate Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who displayed AI-generated images of his imprisoned father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, at his party's convention in July. The court voted 4-3 to not punish Bolsonaro, determining the deepfake was used at a private event before his official candidacy announcement rather than as a public political advertisement.

In a separate 5-2 vote, the court defined political deepfakes as synthetic content created through artificial intelligence that realistically reproduces the image, voice, or speech of any person. These new standards will govern the vast amount of online campaign content from candidates leading up to the first round of voting on October 4. Broadcasters must allocate significant airtime for candidate advertisements, including 14 minutes daily for nearly 1,000 thirty-second ads.

stories.Headline: Protein Industries Canada invests in AI technology to boost on-farm productivity and bring new solutions to farmers
stories.Summary:
Protein Industries Canada is investing $4.9 million into two artificial intelligence projects designed to help Canadian farmers increase productivity and improve safety. The projects involve partnerships between companies like TerraVision360, Metos Canada, Rocky Mountain Equipment, Super GeoAI Technology Inc., and Southview Farms. The first project will create an AI tool to predict and manage disease risk in pulse crops by analyzing weather and crop data, enabling farmers to apply fungicides more strategically and reduce costs. The second project will develop a drone and LiDAR system to measure grain volumes in storage bins accurately while eliminating the need for dangerous manual climbing.

These investments are part of Canada's effort to advance agricultural innovation and support the adoption of made-in-Canada AI solutions. Government officials emphasized that the projects will strengthen farm competitiveness, reduce operational risks, and enhance worker safety across the agriculture sector. The funding comes through the Pan-Canadian Artificial Intelligence Strategy and supports the broader goal of growing Canada's plant-based food and ingredient industry to $25 billion.

Indian Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Jitin Prasada attended the G20 Innovation Ministerial in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, where he met with global leaders and technology executives. He held bilateral discussions with U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, focusing on deepening cooperation between India and the United States in semiconductors, artificial intelligence, and data centers. Prasada also engaged with Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown to discuss advances and policy directions in artificial intelligence.

During the event, Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang praised India's information technology industry. Prasada responded by crediting the nation's prime minister for India's growing leadership in the global technology and artificial intelligence sectors. He emphasized India's commitment to building a strong domestic artificial intelligence ecosystem through its local innovators and youth, highlighting increasing international confidence in the country's technical talent and infrastructure.
